# #8690 PERMANENT-EXCLUSION REGISTER — the classification of every line still in
# compact_block_divergences_2419.txt.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The inventory counts sites that DIVERGE. It says nothing
# about whether a site MAY be normalized, and by the end of the sweep those are
# almost disjoint questions: 47 lines remain and ~43 of them must never be
# normalized. A bare count of 47 reads as 47 units of work, and the only way to
# "finish" it is to normalize sites the guards exist to protect. This file is
# what the inventory's remainder actually means.
#
# FORMAT: <site>\t<class>\t<reason>
#
# CLASSES
#   partial          something already consumes part of the tail. Truncating it
#                    removes a value that is READ, on a config that commits
#                    clean. Forbidden to every scope by
#                    TestNormalizerScopeNeverCoversAPartialSite8690.
#
#                    #8933 NARROWED WHAT THIS CLASS ENTITLES YOU TO CONCLUDE.
#                    "Partial" is a measurement that something consumed the
#                    tail. It is NOT a finding that the consumer is entitled
#                    to it. The eight `policy-options ... term <t> then
#                    <action>` entries that stood here were partial because
#                    the compiler packed the action name into
#                    PolicyTerm.Action -- losing the value AND the term's
#                    terminal action, so the term stopped terminating. The
#                    consumer WAS the defect; removing it made all eight
#                    equivalent, verified across the multi-token tails too
#                    (`community add <v>`, `community delete [ a b ]`,
#                    `as-path-prepend "<asn> <asn>"`). They were removed from
#                    this register by #8933, not deleted silently.
#
#                    So before classing a site partial FOREVER, ask what reads
#                    the tail and whether it should. And do not build a control
#                    on the assumption that a partial site can never be
#                    normalized -- the #2419 positive-control anchor was chosen
#                    on exactly that premise and #8933 consumed it.
#   gate-open-question
#                    the disarm arm reds here: rejected at strict commit with the
#                    pass disabled, accepted with it enabled. THAT IS A QUESTION,
#                    NOT A VERDICT, and this register got it wrong at first by
#                    recording such reds as permanent.
#                    The arm cannot distinguish a gate refusing the packed
#                    SPELLING (harmful to disarm) from one refusing the
#                    CONSEQUENCE OF THE DROP — where the pass repairs the drop
#                    and the acceptance is correct. Only a person can, and the
#                    verdict's home is the `benign` map in
#                    compact_normalize_scope_8690_test.go.
#                    PROOF THAT THIS DISTINCTION IS LOAD-BEARING: `security ipsec
#                    policy <p> proposal-set` and its ike collateral were listed
#                    here as permanent on this arm's red alone. Classified, they
#                    were BENIGN — the gate refuses the dropped proposal-set and
#                    says so in its own message — and they normalized in
#                    0c4818aa0. Two of the entries this register called permanent
#                    were available work.
#                    So these are NOT permanent. They are unanswered questions,
#                    and answering one is the available work.
#   gate-confirmed   classified BY A PERSON as a genuine disarm, with the
#                    evidence. Permanent. Currently empty: no site here has been
#                    carried through step 3.
#   gate-collateral  not itself gate-disarming, but shares a (container, head)
#                    pair with a `gate` site, and the predicate's two arguments
#                    cannot express the difference. Lost with the pair.
#   unmeasurable     the census fixture cannot produce a type-valid value, so
#                    gate status cannot be measured. NOT known-safe.
#   unreachable      no (container, head) rule can express it — the container is
#                    wildcard-named, so production passes an arbitrary instance
#                    name where a rule would need a keyword.
#   sibling-blocked  MEASURED, with the pair ADMITTED and the pass both enabled
#                    and disabled, to change NOTHING at the commit boundary: the
#                    pass splits the tail correctly and a required sibling the
#                    compact spelling cannot carry is still missing, so the same
#                    gate fires either way.
#
#                    Deliberately NOT `unreachable`, which is about a rule's
#                    expressiveness — a wildcard-named container a (container,
#                    head) pair cannot name. This is about the CONFIG SHAPE: the
#                    rule can name it perfectly well and normalizing it would
#                    still accomplish nothing. Same conclusion, different reason,
#                    and collapsing them would lose which wall a future reader is
#                    standing at. The required-sibling wall is the one #8725
#                    turns on; the expressiveness wall is not.
#
#                    NOT `unmeasurable`: these WERE measured. The distinction
#                    that matters is that a sibling in this class was measured
#                    SEPARATELY rather than inheriting a family verdict — nine of
#                    the ten rpm-test leaves would have inherited `test <t>
#                    target`'s benign verdict under any family-level judgement,
#                    and none of them shares it.
#   hazard           normalizing breaks documented, shipped behaviour that no
#                    disarm measurement detects.
#   open             genuinely available work with no gate in the way.
#   wrong-remedy     normalizing this site does NOT fix its defect, and admitting
#                    it would remove inventory lines while the reachable harm is
#                    untouched. Permanent for the count, but for a reason unlike
#                    the others: not forbidden (`partial`), not a no-op
#                    (`no-drop-measured`), not inert at the boundary
#                    (`sibling-blocked`) -- a FALSE FIX, which changes something,
#                    onto the wrong object. The entry must name the real defect
#                    and cite the cell showing the remedy missing its target.
#   no-drop-measured MEASURED, at every reachable spelling, to drop nothing. The
#                    pass is not load-bearing here in either direction, so there
#                    is no fix to make and no behaviour to change. Distinct from
#                    `unmeasurable`, whose reason is a fixture limitation that
#                    evaporates the moment someone improves the fixture; this
#                    reason does not. Evidence is executable, not prose:
#                    compact_scheduler_name_measured_8690_test.go.
#
#                    THIS CLASS REPLACED `owed-own-change`, WHICH EXISTED FOR
#                    ONE HOUR AND HELD ONLY THESE TWO SITES. That class was
#                    created to hold an argument I reasoned out and did not run:
#                    that a packed `scheduler-name` is silently dropped, leaving
#                    a PERMANENTLY-ACTIVE security policy, so normalizing it was
#                    a correct fix owing a failover smoke. Measured, every clause
#                    is false. The argument was built on a spelling nobody
#                    writes: I reasoned about a hierarchical brace-elided form
#                    instead of running the flat `set` form operators actually
#                    use. A measurement of the wrong spelling is not a weaker
#                    measurement, it is a measurement of a different question.
#   unclassified     in another lane's family and NOT measured here. Deliberately
#                    distinct from `open`: "nobody has checked" is a third state,
#                    and recording it as available asserts a measurement that was
#                    not taken.
#
# THIS REGISTER WAS WRONG TWICE IN ITS FIRST HOUR, BOTH TIMES IN THE
# OVER-RESTRICTIVE DIRECTION, AND BOTH ERRORS HAD THE SAME SHAPE: a result
# established at one granularity, recorded at a finer one.
#
#   `security ipsec policy <p> proposal-set` (+ its ike collateral) were listed
#   permanent on the DISARM ARM'S RED. That red is a question, not a verdict —
#   the arm cannot tell a gate refusing the packed spelling from one refusing
#   the CONSEQUENCE of the drop. Classified by a person, they were BENIGN, and
#   they normalized in 0c4818aa0.
#
#   `chassis device-map interface` / `unmapped-interface-policy` were listed
#   `hazard` on a PER-FAMILY bisection: admitting every chassis pair reds three
#   redundancy-group cells. True of the family; not true of these two sites,
#   whose pairs are different. Measured per site they are safe, and they
#   normalized alongside schedulers.
#
# Four sites this file called permanent were available work. The lesson is the
# one the sweep has been applying everywhere else and this register did not:
# CHECK PER SITE, NOT PER FAMILY — and treat an instrument's red as the
# question it is until a person answers it.
#
# SITES ARRIVE AS WELL AS LEAVE, and the register has to carry both. Twelve
# entered between the #8729 measurement and this file landing — ten `services
# rpm probe` leaves and two `policies ... scheduler-name` — not because a
# compact-blind reader was introduced, but because another lane's
# value-synthesis work made them OBSERVABLE to the census. `schedulers scheduler
# <s> {start,stop}-date` arrived the same way mid-flight and moved a measured
# family from 21 sites to 23.
#
# A blind-spot count that RISES is the instrument improving, and the register
# must not treat an arrival as a defect. What it must do is refuse to let one
# pass unclassified, which is what the set-equality assertion does.
#
# EVERY MEASUREMENT NAMES THE COMMIT IT WAS TAKEN AT, and that is not
# bookkeeping. Two classifications in this register described sites that had
# already left the inventory by the time anyone read them — a reader checking
# the file finds nothing and cannot tell whether the site was fixed or was never
# there. A verdict about a live artefact is only meaningful with its `as-of`.
#
# AND EVERY VERDICT HERE IS CONDITIONAL ON THE SCOPE AT THAT COMMIT. A
# `gate-confirmed` or benign classification says what WOULD happen if the pair
# were admitted; none of these pairs is admitted today, so nothing in this file
# describes a live defect. Writing "is a disarm" where the evidence says "would
# be a disarm if admitted" is the difference between a hole in the tree and a
# hole caught before it was opened — this register only ever records the second.
#
# THIS FILE IS A GATE, NOT A REGISTRY. The guard asserts set-equality with the
# inventory in BOTH directions, and drives every non-`open` site through the
# real normalizer to confirm the pass still leaves it alone. A listed site that
# becomes admissible reds; an inventory site missing from this file reds. An
# exclusion list that only accumulates is a place to hide defects.

#
# CHOOSING A CONTROL THAT SURVIVES THE NEXT WIDENING (#8936 item 3).
#
# Do NOT anchor a control on a site because its drop shape is `partial`. That
# argument was tried and failed three times: `partial` measures that SOMETHING
# CONSUMED THE TAIL, and the consumer can be the DEFECT rather than a reader
# entitled to it -- so the site becomes normalizable the moment the defect is
# fixed, and the anchor is consumed by the next family to land.
#
# Audited across all 13 partial sites (#8936): none was excluded because a
# legitimate reader consumes the tail. The last one that was load-bearing,
# `tunnel routing-instance destination`, turned out to be a defect the class was
# protecting -- the elided spelling compiled RoutingInstance="destination"
# instead of the operator's instance name -- and it is fixed, so it has left
# this register entirely.
#
# ANCHOR ON AN INSTANCE-NAME SLOT INSTEAD. A site whose CONTAINER slot is an
# arbitrary instance name (`interfaces <if> mtu`, `bridge-domains <bd>
# routing-interface`) cannot be reached by a (container keyword, head) predicate
# at all, because production calls it with node.Keys[0] and no static pair can
# name an operator-chosen string. That is a permanent bound of the pair-keyed
# design (#8921), not a classification a fix can dissolve.
bridge-domains xpfname domain-type	partial	drop shape "partial" in the inventory
bridge-domains xpfname routing-interface	partial	drop shape "partial" in the inventory
class-of-service schedulers xpfarg surplus-sharing	open	NEWLY VISIBLE, not newly broken (#9056 valueless-flag site model). This site is a VALUELESS BOOLEAN LEAF -- args:0, no wildcard, no children -- and the #2419 census admitted a site only when the head declared an `args` token or a wildcard, so the shape satisfied none of the three arms, was never enumerated, appeared in no skip bucket, and its absence was indistinguishable from a clean verdict. The census now enumerates it with a PRESENCE discriminator (`stanza { flag; }` against `stanza { }`, compactSite.flag); 511 flag sites, 93 divergent, of which the 19 in the `security` subtree were normalized by this change and these 74 remain. Classified `open` because they are ordinary brace-elided drops with nothing protecting them: every one measures drop shape `empty` -- a positive measurement that no reader consumes the packed tail -- and the elided spelling is SILENT at the strict commit gate (accepted, and emitting no FEWER diagnostics than the braced spelling), so admitting the pair converts a silent drop into a correct compile rather than quieting a signal the operator already gets. NOT yet assessed against the normalizer's per-pair admission rules: whoever takes them owes the #8921 collision check per pair -- several of these heads sit under containers that repeat across the schema, e.g. `then discard` under BOTH `firewall policer` and `firewall three-color-policer`, and every `protocols ...` head is declared twice because `routing-instances <n> protocols` mirrors it -- and a re-measurement at their own HEAD.

NOT yet assessed against the normalizer's per-pair admission rules: whoever takes them owes the #8921 collision check per pair -- several of these heads sit under containers that repeat across the schema, e.g. `then discard` under BOTH `firewall policer` and `firewall three-color-policer`, and every `protocols ...` head is declared twice because `routing-instances <n> protocols` mirrors it -- and a re-measurement at their own HEAD. SPELLING BOUND (#8755, RE-MEASURED at 1748e11a2 for this site rather than inherited): the bound recorded on the older `family inet` entries in this file -- that the pass never traverses into a braced multi-key container, so `family inet { <leaf> ...; }` is UNREACHABLE to a (container, head) rule -- DOES NOT HOLD any more. #8763 taught normalizeCompactNodes to descend a compoundKey node, and the pass now asks a pair for every losing spelling of this site. Measured by running the real pass with a recording predicate: `family inet { sampling input; }` asks ("sampling","input"); `family inet sampling input;` and `family { inet sampling input; }` both ask ("inet","sampling"); `family inet targeted-broadcast;` and `family { inet targeted-broadcast; }` ask ("inet","targeted-broadcast"); `family inet { address 10.0.0.1/24 preferred; }` asks ("address","preferred"); `firewall family inet { filter f1 interface-specific; }` asks ("filter","interface-specific"). Every one of those spellings still DROPS the value today, so the work is available and `open` means available AND reachable here -- but it is two or three pair admissions per site, not one, because the elided-`family` spellings resolve to a different pair from the elided-child one. The stale bound on the neighbouring entries is filed as issue 9446.

firewall policer xpfarg logical-interface-policer	open	NEWLY VISIBLE, not newly broken (#9056 valueless-flag site model). This site is a VALUELESS BOOLEAN LEAF -- args:0, no wildcard, no children -- and the #2419 census admitted a site only when the head declared an `args` token or a wildcard, so the shape satisfied none of the three arms, was never enumerated, appeared in no skip bucket, and its absence was indistinguishable from a clean verdict. The census now enumerates it with a PRESENCE discriminator (`stanza { flag; }` against `stanza { }`, compactSite.flag); 511 flag sites, 93 divergent, of which the 19 in the `security` subtree were normalized by this change and these 74 remain. Classified `open` because they are ordinary brace-elided drops with nothing protecting them: every one measures drop shape `empty` -- a positive measurement that no reader consumes the packed tail -- and the elided spelling is SILENT at the strict commit gate (accepted, and emitting no FEWER diagnostics than the braced spelling), so admitting the pair converts a silent drop into a correct compile rather than quieting a signal the operator already gets. NOT yet assessed against the normalizer's per-pair admission rules: whoever takes them owes the #8921 collision check per pair -- several of these heads sit under containers that repeat across the schema, e.g. `then discard` under BOTH `firewall policer` and `firewall three-color-policer`, and every `protocols ...` head is declared twice because `routing-instances <n> protocols` mirrors it -- and a re-measurement at their own HEAD.

NOT yet assessed against the normalizer's per-pair admission rules: whoever takes them owes the #8921 collision check per pair -- several of these heads sit under containers that repeat across the schema, e.g. `then discard` under BOTH `firewall policer` and `firewall three-color-policer`, and every `protocols ...` head is declared twice because `routing-instances <n> protocols` mirrors it -- and a re-measurement at their own HEAD.

interfaces xpfname unit xpfarg family inet address xpfarg vrrp-group	open	NEWLY VISIBLE, not newly broken (#8690 instance-name model). The census named every instance `xpfarg`, and `unit` declares a NUMBER — so the compiler dropped the whole unit and every site beneath it recorded `leaf value not observable`, a verdict about the site MODEL rather than the leaf. With schema-derived instance names 69 of the 236 not-observable sites became observable and these 24 are the divergent ones, all under `interfaces <if> unit <u>`. Classified `open` because they are ordinary brace-elided drops with nothing protecting them: measured by hand, `family inet address 10.0.0.1/24;` compiles to NO address and `filter input f1;` binds NO filter, both on a strict commit reporting success with fewer warnings than the correct spelling. The flat-set `set` form is unaffected; the loss is the hierarchical brace-elided spelling a config file / `load override` / peer-sync payload carries. NOT yet assessed against the normalizer's admission rules — whoever takes them owes the packed-tail and disarm checks per site. SPELLING BOUND (#8755, measured at 769f2f622): a scope entry closes ONE of four losing spellings. Compiled through the real pass under the production scope: `family inet { filter { input f4; } }` keeps the value (fully braced, correct); `family inet filter input f4;` is DROPPED and is the only form a chain admission reaches; `family inet { filter input f4; }` is DROPPED and is UNREACHABLE — the pass never traverses into a braced multi-key container, because normalizeCompactNodes recurses with schema.children["family"] while those children belong to `family inet`, advancing the schema one level where the node advanced two (pairsAsked=[] for that shape under admit-all). `family { inet { ... } }` and `family { inet ... }` are dropped too. So `open` here means AVAILABLE, not FULLY FIXABLE: normalizing this site leaves the idiomatic braced-family elision losing its value. `unit`-level sites (description, vlan-id, inner-vlan-id) are NOT subject to this — their second token is an instance arg consumed by `identity`, not a child keyword. POPULATION (#8755, measured at 0ab895a56 over test/incus/*.conf + docs/*.conf, 8 files): braced `family inet {` = 77, packed `family inet <keyword>` = 0. The scope entry reaches ONLY the packed spelling, so it would fix a form with NO instances in the corpus while the form with 77 stays unreachable until #8763. `open` here therefore means AVAILABLE, not ADDRESSING-OBSERVED-EXPOSURE. Eight test and doc configs are not customer configs — absence is evidence, not proof — and three lanes measuring this got 77 / 104 / 144 by different corpora and patterns, unanimous on the shape. TestNoShippedConfigUsesThePackedFamilySpelling_8755 reds if a packed spelling ever appears, which would give the remedy a population and require re-reading this note.

The scope entry reaches ONLY the packed spelling, so it would fix a form with NO instances in the corpus while the form with 77 stays unreachable until #8763. `open` here therefore means AVAILABLE, not ADDRESSING-OBSERVED-EXPOSURE. Eight test and doc configs are not customer configs — absence is evidence, not proof — and three lanes measuring this got 77 / 104 / 144 by different corpora and patterns, unanimous on the shape. TestNoShippedConfigUsesThePackedFamilySpelling_8755 reds if a packed spelling ever appears, which would give the remedy a population and require re-reading this note.
interfaces xpfname unit xpfarg family inet dhcp retransmission-interval	open	NEWLY VISIBLE, not newly broken (#8690 instance-name model). The census named every instance `xpfarg`, and `unit` declares a NUMBER — so the compiler dropped the whole unit and every site beneath it recorded `leaf value not observable`, a verdict about the site MODEL rather than the leaf. With schema-derived instance names 69 of the 236 not-observable sites became observable and these 24 are the divergent ones, all under `interfaces <if> unit <u>`. Classified `open` because they are ordinary brace-elided drops with nothing protecting them: measured by hand, `family inet address 10.0.0.1/24;` compiles to NO address and `filter input f1;` binds NO filter, both on a strict commit reporting success with fewer warnings than the correct spelling. The flat-set `set` form is unaffected; the loss is the hierarchical brace-elided spelling a config file / `load override` / peer-sync payload carries. NOT yet assessed against the normalizer's admission rules — whoever takes them owes the packed-tail and disarm checks per site. SPELLING BOUND (#8755, measured at 769f2f622): a scope entry closes ONE of four losing spellings. Compiled through the real pass under the production scope: `family inet { filter { input f4; } }` keeps the value (fully braced, correct); `family inet filter input f4;` is DROPPED and is the only form a chain admission reaches; `family inet { filter input f4; }` is DROPPED and is UNREACHABLE — the pass never traverses into a braced multi-key container, because normalizeCompactNodes recurses with schema.children["family"] while those children belong to `family inet`, advancing the schema one level where the node advanced two (pairsAsked=[] for that shape under admit-all). `family { inet { ... } }` and `family { inet ... }` are dropped too. So `open` here means AVAILABLE, not FULLY FIXABLE: normalizing this site leaves the idiomatic braced-family elision losing its value. `unit`-level sites (description, vlan-id, inner-vlan-id) are NOT subject to this — their second token is an instance arg consumed by `identity`, not a child keyword. interfaces xpfname unit xpfarg family inet sampling input	open	NEWLY VISIBLE, not newly broken (#9056 valueless-flag site model). This site is a VALUELESS BOOLEAN LEAF -- args:0, no wildcard, no children -- and the #2419 census admitted a site only when the head declared an `args` token or a wildcard, so the shape satisfied none of the three arms, was never enumerated, appeared in no skip bucket, and its absence was indistinguishable from a clean verdict. The census now enumerates it with a PRESENCE discriminator (`stanza { flag; }` against `stanza { }`, compactSite.flag); 511 flag sites, 93 divergent, of which the 19 in the `security` subtree were normalized by this change and these 74 remain. Classified `open` because they are ordinary brace-elided drops with nothing protecting them: every one measures drop shape `empty` -- a positive measurement that no reader consumes the packed tail -- and the elided spelling is SILENT at the strict commit gate (accepted, and emitting no FEWER diagnostics than the braced spelling), so admitting the pair converts a silent drop into a correct compile rather than quieting a signal the operator already gets. NOT yet assessed against the normalizer's per-pair admission rules: whoever takes them owes the #8921 collision check per pair -- several of these heads sit under containers that repeat across the schema, e.g. `then discard` under BOTH `firewall policer` and `firewall three-color-policer`, and every `protocols ...` head is declared twice because `routing-instances <n> protocols` mirrors it -- and a re-measurement at their own HEAD. SPELLING BOUND (#8755, RE-MEASURED at 1748e11a2 for this site rather than inherited): the bound recorded on the older `family inet` entries in this file -- that the pass never traverses into a braced multi-key container, so `family inet { <leaf> ...; }` is UNREACHABLE to a (container, head) rule -- DOES NOT HOLD any more. #8763 taught normalizeCompactNodes to descend a compoundKey node, and the pass now asks a pair for every losing spelling of this site. Measured by running the real pass with a recording predicate: `family inet { sampling input; }` asks ("sampling","input"); `family inet sampling input;` and `family { inet sampling input; }` both ask ("inet","sampling"); `family inet targeted-broadcast;` and `family { inet targeted-broadcast; }` ask ("inet","targeted-broadcast"); `family inet { address 10.0.0.1/24 preferred; }` asks ("address","preferred"); `firewall family inet { filter f1 interface-specific; }` asks ("filter","interface-specific"). Every one of those spellings still DROPS the value today, so the work is available and `open` means available AND reachable here -- but it is two or three pair admissions per site, not one, because the elided-`family` spellings resolve to a different pair from the elided-child one. The stale bound on the neighbouring entries is filed as issue 9446.

Compiled through the real pass under the production scope: `family inet { filter { input f4; } }` keeps the value (fully braced, correct); `family inet filter input f4;` is DROPPED and is the only form a chain admission reaches; `family inet { filter input f4; }` is DROPPED and is UNREACHABLE — the pass never traverses into a braced multi-key container, because normalizeCompactNodes recurses with schema.children["family"] while those children belong to `family inet`, advancing the schema one level where the node advanced two (pairsAsked=[] for that shape under admit-all). `family { inet { ... } }` and `family { inet ... }` are dropped too. So `open` here means AVAILABLE, not FULLY FIXABLE: normalizing this site leaves the idiomatic braced-family elision losing its value. `unit`-level sites (description, vlan-id, inner-vlan-id) are NOT subject to this — their second token is an instance arg consumed by `identity`, not a child keyword. POPULATION (#8755, measured at 0ab895a56 over test/incus/*.conf + docs/*.conf, 8 files): braced `family inet {` = 77, packed `family inet <keyword>` = 0. The scope entry reaches ONLY the packed spelling, so it would fix a form with NO instances in the corpus while the form with 77 stays unreachable until #8763. `open` here therefore means AVAILABLE, not ADDRESSING-OBSERVED-EXPOSURE. Eight test and doc configs are not customer configs — absence is evidence, not proof — and three lanes measuring this got 77 / 104 / 144 by different corpora and patterns, unanimous on the shape. TestNoShippedConfigUsesThePackedFamilySpelling_8755 reds if a packed spelling ever appears, which would give the remedy a population and require re-reading this note.

interfaces xpfname unit xpfarg family inet6 sampling input	open	NEWLY VISIBLE, not newly broken (#9056 valueless-flag site model). This site is a VALUELESS BOOLEAN LEAF -- args:0, no wildcard, no children -- and the #2419 census admitted a site only when the head declared an `args` token or a wildcard, so the shape satisfied none of the three arms, was never enumerated, appeared in no skip bucket, and its absence was indistinguishable from a clean verdict. The census now enumerates it with a PRESENCE discriminator (`stanza { flag; }` against `stanza { }`, compactSite.flag); 511 flag sites, 93 divergent, of which the 19 in the `security` subtree were normalized by this change and these 74 remain. Classified `open` because they are ordinary brace-elided drops with nothing protecting them: every one measures drop shape `empty` -- a positive measurement that no reader consumes the packed tail -- and the elided spelling is SILENT at the strict commit gate (accepted, and emitting no FEWER diagnostics than the braced spelling), so admitting the pair converts a silent drop into a correct compile rather than quieting a signal the operator already gets. NOT yet assessed against the normalizer's per-pair admission rules: whoever takes them owes the #8921 collision check per pair -- several of these heads sit under containers that repeat across the schema, e.g. `then discard` under BOTH `firewall policer` and `firewall three-color-policer`, and every `protocols ...` head is declared twice because `routing-instances <n> protocols` mirrors it -- and a re-measurement at their own HEAD. SPELLING BOUND (#8755, RE-MEASURED at 1748e11a2 for this site rather than inherited): the bound recorded on the older `family inet` entries in this file -- that the pass never traverses into a braced multi-key container, so `family inet { <leaf> ...; }` is UNREACHABLE to a (container, head) rule -- DOES NOT HOLD any more. #8763 taught normalizeCompactNodes to descend a compoundKey node, and the pass now asks a pair for every losing spelling of this site. Measured by running the real pass with a recording predicate: `family inet { sampling input; }` asks ("sampling","input"); `family inet sampling input;` and `family { inet sampling input; }` both ask ("inet","sampling"); `family inet targeted-broadcast;` and `family { inet targeted-broadcast; }` ask ("inet","targeted-broadcast"); `family inet { address 10.0.0.1/24 preferred; }` asks ("address","preferred"); `firewall family inet { filter f1 interface-specific; }` asks ("filter","interface-specific"). Every one of those spellings still DROPS the value today, so the work is available and `open` means available AND reachable here -- but it is two or three pair admissions per site, not one, because the elided-`family` spellings resolve to a different pair from the elided-child one. The stale bound on the neighbouring entries is filed as issue 9446.

interfaces xpfname vlan-tagging	partial	drop shape "partial" in the inventory (#9056 valueless-flag site, newly enumerated). security policies from-zone xpfarg xpfarg xpfarg policy xpfarg scheduler-name	open	SUPERSEDED BY #8752 -- reclassified from `wrong-remedy` to `open`. Cite: scheduler_name_forwarding_8690_test.go and flat_set_merges_hierarchical_duplicates_test.go (both runnable). The `wrong-remedy` verdict rested on one fact that is no longer true: that normalizing moved the packed tail into a SPURIOUS DUPLICATE policy, restoring the schedule onto the wrong object. #8752 folds a repeated `policy <p>` statement into the first occurrence on the tolerant path, so that duplicate no longer exists. MEASURED AFTER THE FOLD: the reachable duplicate spelling (`policy p1 { match ... then permit; } policy p1 scheduler-name S;`) now compiles on the LENIENT path to ONE policy -- sched="S", match criteria intact, action PERMIT -- so the harm this entry described (a policy written TIME-LIMITED running PERMANENTLY ACTIVE) is fixed WITHOUT the normalizer: the fold carries the packed tail onto the surviving policy itself. WHAT REMAINS is a genuine, narrower divergence, measured at the census's own shape: a LONE `policy p1 scheduler-name S;` with no sibling compiles with sched="" where the block spelling `policy p1 { scheduler-name S; }` compiles with sched="S". The site still drops, and the remedy now lands on the RIGHT object because there is no other policy for it to land on -- ordinary available work rather than a false fix, which is what `open` means. NOT ADMITTED HERE: widening still owes the #8690 two-arm procedure (arm 1, no reader consumes the tail; arm 2, the strict-path acceptance comparison), and neither was re-run after the fold; this entry records that the obstacle changed, not that the work is done. CLASS HISTORY, kept because this entry has been wrong three times: `owed-own-change` (an argument reasoned and never run) -> `no-drop-measured` (a strict-path measurement, correct and insufficient -- the strict path REJECTS the elided spelling, so cfg is nil and a gate firing is the ABSENCE of a compiled result, not evidence about one) -> `wrong-remedy` (a lenient-path measurement, true until #8752 removed its premise) -> `open`
security policies from-zone xpfarg xpfarg xpfarg policy xpfarg then permit	gate-open-question	#9056 valueless-flag site, newly enumerated, and the NEGATIVE CONTROL for that family. The leaf is a valueless flag of exactly the shape normalized elsewhere in this change, and it is DELIBERATELY not admitted: measured on a complete policy fixture (`policy p1 { match { source-address any; destination-address any; application any; } then permit; }`), the braced spelling is ACCEPTED at the strict commit gate and the elided spelling is REJECTED by the #3043 terminal-action gate -- `global policy "p1": no terminal action; every policy must specify exactly one of `then permit`, `then deny`, or `then reject``. Admitting the pair would convert a LOUD rejection into a silent acceptance, which is the #8868 regression-wearing-the-shape-of-a-fix. `gate-open-question` rather than `gate-confirmed` because the #3043 gate refuses the CONSEQUENCE of the drop (a policy with no terminal action), not the packed SPELLING: if the pass repaired the drop the acceptance would be correct, so this is a red that is available work until somebody answers it -- and answering it owes the #8921 collision check, since `reject` is declared under seven `then` containers and `permit` under two. TestPolicyTerminalActionElisionStaysRejected9056 pins the rejection so the exclusion cannot be reversed silently.

Observable only in a config where the test already has a target from another statement, which the compact spelling cannot carry — the same required-sibling wall #8725 turns on. Observable only in a config where the test already has a target from another statement, which the compact spelling cannot carry — the same required-sibling wall #8725 turns on.
